articles.title: China factory inflation hits 5%, fastest in over four years, as CPI lags at 0.9%
articles.expand: The gap between surging factory prices and subdued consumer inflation points to an oil-driven cost shock, not demand-led inflation. That makes crude and commodity prices the main driver of China’s price data for now. China moving from exporting disinflation to passing on higher costs adds to global goods-price pressure, which is unwelcome for central banks already worried about energy-driven inflation, including the Fed and ECB . The weak yen is the key amplifier: with oil prices elevated by the Iran war, every leg lower in the currency raises the yen cost of energy and feeds back into pipeline inflation.
